text:
incident-bot: P99 latency breach detected for /v1/stream (usw2). p95=320ms (SLO=200ms), p99=1.8s (SLO=400ms) — paging oncall
ops-bot: paging maya (oncall) :rotating_light:
maya (oncall): seeing it, joining. any customer pages?
paul (customer-ops): got 2 reports from PartnerX complaining about interactive streaming stalls around 11:04. They say streaming takeovers time out mid-response.
maya (oncall): thanks @paul. quick check of metrics: continous-batching path showing elevated tail latency. mixed sequence-length queues spiking.
arjun (eng-runtime): confirmed on dashboards — continuous-batcher CPU/TX hotspots + KV cache misses rising. Looks like long sequences are causing large batches to block short streaming requests.
lina (sre): is this specific to a model or all streaming models?
arjun (eng-runtime): mostly gpt-mid and gpt-small variants on cont-batch; streaming route shows queue depth jump from 40 -> 420 in 30s. batch sizes up to 128 when long seqs included.
maya (oncall): immediate mitigation options?
arjun (eng-runtime): quick mitigations: 1) enable batch-size cap for streaming route (max_batch=16). 2) enable preemptive-shed for long seqs: drop into dedicated slow-path. 3) route streaming to dedicated pool with lower pack-window. I can flip 1 & 2 now.
maya (oncall): do it. call out commands / config please.
arjun (eng-runtime): running config rollout:
```
PATCH /config/routes/streaming
body: {"batching": {"max_batch": 16, "pack_window_ms": 8}, "preemptive_shed": true}
```
Applied to canary subset (usw2-a).
ops-bot: deploybot: rolling config to usw2-a -> success
maya (oncall): monitoring p95/p99 after canary. Lina, Paul — can you watch customer reports?
lina (sre): watching traces. starting distributed traces filter by request_id prefix from PartnerX.
paul (customer-ops): pinged PartnerX: lowered impact after 20:20 UTC. they still see occasional stalls but much better.
arjun (eng-runtime): canary looks promising: p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 420ms in canary shard. but global still shows tail at ~1.2s because not all nodes updated and queued long sequences continue to leak.
maya (oncall): plan to roll to full region? any risk?
arjun (eng-runtime): main risk: increasing small-request throughput might slightly raise CPU due to smaller packing efficiency. but safer for latency. recommend full rollout to region. I'll start rolling to usw2-b then usw2-c.
ops-bot: deploybot: rolling to usw2-b -> success
ops-bot: deploybot: rolling to usw2-c -> success
maya (oncall): roll complete. p95 now 210ms, p99 380ms — within SLO window trending down. great.
paul (customer-ops): PartnerX confirmed improvement, still monitoring.
lina (sre): follow-up tasks: 1) add per-seq-length weighting to batch scheduler (lower priority for long sequences). 2) add KV cache warmup for known long sessions. 3) create alert for batch-size amplification (when avg_batch_size > 64 and p99>800ms).
arjun (eng-runtime): agree. I'll open runtime PR with scheduler fairness weights and add config toggle for seq-length thresholds. also recommend a controlled experiment to tune max_batch between 8-24 for streaming workload.
maya (oncall): handoff: I'm handing to arjun for postmortem and remediation. Oncall clear for live incident, but please treat as Sev2 follow-up.
arjun (eng-runtime): taking ownership for follow-up. I'll post a short incident notes doc and link evals for model patterns triggering amplification.
paul (customer-ops): noting customer impact: PartnerX had 2 affected sessions 11:04-11:12 UTC, degraded UX for ~8m. No data loss, just stalls.
lina (sre): capturing commands/rollouts in incident log. recommended timeline entry:
- 11:04 alert -> p99 1.8s
- 11:09 canary config (max_batch=16, preemptive_shed=true)
- 11:12 canary success, partial improvement
- 11:15 full rollout complete, p99 within SLO
maya (oncall): thanks team. arjun, please add remediation ticket and assign owners for scheduler change, KV warmup, and alert tuning. I'll close paging after postmortem is linked.
arjun (eng-runtime): will do. filing tickets now.
ops-bot: incident closed (notes pending)
maya (oncall): closing thread, leaving postmortem to arjun + lina. thanks all :thumbsup:
